trigger: Rebuild() throws after line 119 (`var a = Attach(e)`): line 120 `Check(e, a)` (Budget/health), line 121 `Apply`/`Check` during replay, or line 122 `replay_mismatch`. Budget() at line 116 runs before the objects are created, so it is not one of these paths.
consequence: The ChoicePolicyAdapter created at 119 (and the MatchEngine created at 117) is never disposed. The callers' `using var trialAdapter = rebuilt.Adapter` (145) and `using var replayAdapter = Rebuild().Adapter` (163) never bind because Rebuild never returns. One adapter leaks per failed candidate probe and per failed prefix replay; failure is a normal path (Budget, replay verification), so leaks accumulate across candidates and steps.

trigger: Any candidate probe in the model branch (line 144) that is evaluated by the inline TrainingAdmission.Check at 149-151.
consequence: The same predicate is written twice with different arguments: Health passes `KLink.Bot.Effects.Blueprint.KismetLibrary.Default is not null` at position 6, the candidate probe passes the literal `true`. The two admission results can diverge (when the blueprint singleton is null the probe admits a state that Health rejects), so Accepted/Rejected and the recorded fault set depend on which call site ran. At most one of the two spellings can match the intended contract.

trigger: Health is called at 128 (zero steps), 121 (during replay) and 161 (after every executed step); the final check at 168-170 runs on the finished state.
consequence: Health passes the literal `Side.Left` for the position where the final call passes `engine.State.Winner`, and the literal `1` where the final call passes `tape.Count`. After the first step the intermediate checks therefore evaluate a step count of 1 for a game with N steps, and they evaluate a fixed Left side for states where the decisive side is not Left. Intermediate and final admission are not the same predicate, so `Admitted`, `Comparable` and `LeftWinDelta` can flip depending on which check produced the reason.

trigger: Elapsed time crosses max-seconds during the step that finishes the game: `Apply(engine, step)` at 161 completes the terminal position, then `Check(engine, adapter)` calls Budget() (107 via 110-111) and throws.
consequence: A game that ran to completion within max-steps is recorded with reason `InvalidOperationException:time_limit` and `Admitted = false`, which forces `Comparable = false` and `LeftWinDelta = null` (92), and prevents the terminal TrainingAdmission.Check at 168 from running at all. The outcome of a completed game is discarded by a clock test that fires after completion; nothing in the report distinguishes this from a genuinely truncated game.

trigger: A finished position whose Winner is neither Left nor Right (draw / None), if the engine can produce one.
consequence: Line 154 records `(score, trial.State.IsFinished, trial.State.Winner == Side.Left)`, so a proven draw becomes Terminal=true, Wins=false: Value() = 0 and Rank() = 0, identical to a proven loss. A completed draw therefore loses every tie at 0 against a non-terminal estimate of 0.0 (line 35 breaks the tie with Rank 1 > 0) and is reported as a non-win in Winner/LeftWinDelta.
dependsOn: Side.Winner can be a non-decisive value while State.IsFinished is true

trigger: policy.Evaluate returns a score greater than 1 for a non-terminal candidate. No range clamp or validation of the model output exists anywhere in this file.
consequence: Value() clamps a terminal win to exactly 1 while a non-terminal entry keeps its raw score, so any non-terminal score > 1 satisfies `next > value` and outranks a proven terminal win; Best returns the undecided continuation instead of the winning one.
dependsOn: policy.Evaluate output range is not bounded to [0,1] by contract
